title: Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For every tree $T$, and every integer $t \geq 1$, if $G$ is a graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $T$, and with no clique of size $t$, then its chromatic number is bounded.
context_text: The Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture, posed independently by Gyárfás and Sumner, asserts that graphs with no induced copy of a fixed tree $T$ and bounded clique number have bounded chromatic number. It has been proved for several families of trees but remains open in general.
paper_contribution: Proves that under the same hypotheses (no clique of size $t$, sufficiently large chromatic number), $G$ contains a path-induced copy of $(T,r)$ for any rooting $r$ of $T$, establishing a weakening of the full conjecture in which induced subgraph containment is replaced by the intermediate notion of path-induced containment.
paper_title: A note on the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture

title: Polynomial bounds for path-induced copy theorem (1.2)
statement_text: For every rooted tree $(T,r)$ and integer $t\ge1$, graphs with no path-induced copy of $(T,r)$ and no clique of size $t$ have bounded chromatic number. Is there any hope for a comparable strengthening of this result, giving a polynomial bound (in $t$) on the chromatic number of graphs with no path-induced copy of a rooted tree $(T,r)$ and with clique number at most $t$?
context_text: The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture says that for every tree $T$ and integer $t\ge1$, graphs with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $T$ and no clique of size $t$ have bounded chromatic number; it is proved for a few families of trees but open in general. A rooted tree $(T,r)$ is a tree $T$ with a distinguished vertex $r$; an isomorphism $\phi$ from $T$ to a (not necessarily induced) subgraph of $G$ is a path-induced copy of $(T,r)$ if for every path $P$ of $T$ with one end $r$, the image of $P$ under $\phi$ is an induced path of $G$ (this lies between subgraph and induced subgraph). The authors prove that the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture holds when excluding a path-induced copy of $(T,r)$ instead of an induced copy of $T$: graphs with no path-induced copy of $(T,r)$ and no clique of size $t$ have chromatic number bounded by a function of $(T,r)$ and $t$. In the analogous setting where $K_{t,t}$ is excluded as a subgraph, Scott, Seymour and Spirkl proved that for every tree $T$ there is a polynomial $f(t)$ such that graphs with no induced $T$ and no $K_{t,t}$ subgraph have average degree at most $f(t)$ (improving Kierstead–Penrice and Rödl). With only bounded clique number one must bound the chromatic number rather than the average degree, since $K_{n,n}$ has no $K_3$ and no path-induced copy of $P_4$; but one can still ask for a polynomial bound. Polynomial bounds in $t$ have recently been shown for a few trees, including every tree that does not contain the five-vertex path $P_5$ as an induced subgraph, but $P_5$ appears to be a sticking point: the best known bound for $P_5$-free graphs of clique number $t$ is the slightly superpolynomial $\chi\le t^{\log_2 t}$. Since a graph contains a path-induced copy of a path rooted at an end if and only if it contains that path as an induced subgraph, polynomial bounds here even for $P_5$ would require improving the $P_5$ bound.

title: Polynomial bounds for the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture
statement_text: It is possible that the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture holds with polynomial bounds; that is, for every tree $T$ there is a polynomial $f$ such that every graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $T$ and no clique of size $t$ has chromatic number at most $f(t)$.
context_text: The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture says that for every tree $T$ and integer $t\ge1$, graphs with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $T$ and no clique of size $t$ have bounded chromatic number; it is proved for a few families of trees but open in general. Polynomial bounds in $t$ have recently been shown for a few trees, including every tree that does not contain the five-vertex path $P_5$ as an induced subgraph, but $P_5$ appears to be a sticking point: the best known bound for $P_5$-free graphs of clique number $t$ is the slightly superpolynomial $\chi\le t^{\log_2 t}$. In the related setting where $K_{t,t}$ is excluded as a subgraph instead of $K_t$, a polynomial bound on the average degree is known (Scott, Seymour and Spirkl). The authors prove the qualitative Gyárfás–Sumner statement for path-induced copies of rooted trees (copies of $T$ in which every path starting at the root is induced), and ask whether polynomial bounds can be obtained there as well.
